newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fixed T-bond yields to ease on large demand.
newsitem.headline: Polish fixed T-bond yields to ease on large demand.

text.p: Polish 15-percent two-year and 12-percent five-year fixed treasury bond yields are expected to fall at Wednesday's 800 million zloty tender, under pressure from large amounts of foreign investor bids, analysts said.

They said average yield of the two-year bond, due on June 12, 1999, should slip below 21 percent from 21.4 percent at the last auction on April 2, in line with falling inflation and dropping yields on treasury bills at recent auctions.

"The two-year bond yield may fall below its market value of around 21 percent to about 20.85-20.9 percent in heavy demand, especially from foreign investors," said Marcin Rzechowski, senior dealer at PBI SA in Warsaw.
Demand at the tender is estimated at up to 1.5 billion zlotys, with foreign bids likely totalling half of that.
Analysts said the average yield of the five-year bond, which matures on June 12, 2002, should form around 18.4 percent, just down from 18.5 percent at last month's tender.
They said bids from Polish banks would be curbed by a severe cash shortage on the local money market caused by short required reserve positions at the start of the month.
"High money market rates may cap Polish banks' demand at the auction, but foreign investors are quite interested in the bonds," said Marta Moscinska, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The value date for the tender is May 12, 1997. Investors may place bids at the tender until 1100 local time (0900 GMT).
